findings.title: Recovery code validation in user storage never consumes the used code
findings.body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks whether the input matches any stored code and never removes or marks the used code as consumed. The authenticator calls isValid and then relies on the stored credential's used state to decide when all codes are spent. Against this provider, a recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, and the test suite cannot detect this. The test provider should either mark codes used or the test should assert single use.

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot remove a federated recovery credential
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated (user storage) credential. When all codes are used, the code calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only targets local storage. For a federated credential the removal is a no-op, so the exhausted credential stays in user storage and the user keeps getting the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action on every login without the credential actually being cleared.

findings.title: Recovery codes written to user storage do not remove the previous local credential
findings.body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, the existing local recovery-codes credential is left untouched, and when it fails the local provider's createCredential is called without first clearing the old one. Regenerating codes can leave stale local credentials alongside the new federated ones. getCredential then returns only the federated one, so the stale local set is silently orphaned, and the state can diverge. Compare with how OTP handling deals with replacement.

findings.title: Stored credential lookup still uses the old path in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls Optional.get() on the result of getCredential without checking presence, so a user with no recovery codes in either store gets a NoSuchElementException while rendering the login form instead of a meaningful error.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences a possibly null MyUser
findings.body: getMyUser(user) can return null when the user is not in the map, and getCredentials then accesses myUser.recoveryCodes and myUser.otp without a null check, causing an NPE. isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream guard against this.

findings.title: Typo in the delayed authenticator config alias
findings.body: The config alias is set to "delayed-suthenticator-config", a misspelling of "authenticator". It is harmless for the test but is a copy error that will confuse anyone searching for the config.

findings.title: Test does not verify that a recovery code is single-use against user storage
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin logs in once with code 0 and checks success, but never checks that the same code is rejected on reuse or that exhausted codes trigger the required action. Given the storage provider never consumes codes, this gap lets the replay bug above go unnoticed.
